answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so each voter’s influence is limited by the walk’s reachable mass. A Sybil cluster behind a sparse external cut has low conductance: few edges carry trust into it, constraining its aggregate voting weight under a fixed start distribution and capped vote rule. The dune, trellis, and fable are metaphors only; the bound follows from the graph’s cut structure.
